verdicts.title: Belyi map for the sporadic group J2
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We present a genus 0 Belyi map for the sporadic Janko group J2 of degree 280. As a consequence we obtain a polynomial having Aut(J2) as a Galois group over K(t) where K is a number field of degree 10.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes 'a genus 0 Belyi map for the sporadic Janko group J2' and a Galois group construction, which shares only the 'Belyi map' vocabulary but does not address tropicalization, Tseitin formulas, or resolution proof depth.

verdicts.title: Belyi map for the sporadic group J1
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We compute the genus 0 Belyi map for the sporadic Janko group J1 of degree 266 and describe the applied method. This yields explicit polynomials having J1 as a Galois group over K(t), [K:Q] = 7.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses a specific Belyi map for the sporadic group J1, which does not interact with the conjecture's claim about tropicalized Belyi functions and resolution proof depth for Tseitin formulas.

verdicts.title: The sporadic group J2, Hauptmodul and Belyi map
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Determining Fourier coefficients of modular forms of a finite index noncongruence subgroups of the modular group is still a non-trivial task. In this brief note we describe a new algorithm to reliably calculate an approximation for a modular form of a given weight.
